{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZkpIzw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhDLOIc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 53, "title": "Correct high-resolution VDP2 rotation-background sampling", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `dacd8b18e2009fb25ed4bcd6fc719d9f796f16f6`, VDP2 rotation backgrounds advance their horizontal source coordinates using every output dot in 640/704-dot modes. `rotation_sample` passes unscaled X into matrix calculations and coefficient lookup; `read_coefficient` likewise multiplies its horizontal increment by that X. The scheduled path supplies an incrementing output coordinate every two main clocks.

Sega’s [VDP2 User’s Manual §2.1, High resolution mode](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p02_10.htm) states that RBG0/RBG1 retain normal-mode horizontal picture resolution. With static identity parameters and effects disabled, a source sequence R,G,B should therefore occupy output dots R,R,G,G,B,B. Current coordinate calculations instead traverse successive source pixels at every output dot. This changes image scale, map boundaries and coefficient progression.

The existing `high_resolution_uses_two_clock_dots_and_rejects_rgb888_rotation` test changes VRAM between acquisitions. It validates retained reads and format restrictions, but does not establish correct static spatial sampling. The normal-resolution guest coverage from #39 also cannot establish this behavior.

## Expected outcome

Implement the documented horizontal sampling of RBG0/RBG1 in standard-TV high-resolution modes, consistently in production scheduled scanout and debugger rendering. Preserve independent output coordinates for windows and composition; avoid resizing the completed framebuffer as a substitute for hardware address generation.

Use these primary contracts together:

- [§2.1](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p02_10.htm): rotation-picture horizontal resolution in high-resolution mode.
- [§6.1](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p06_10.htm), [§6.3](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p06_30.htm) and [§6.4](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p06_40.htm): transformed coordinates, horizontal increments, coefficient addressing and parameter selection.
- [§8.1, including table8.1](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p08_10.htm): window positions use TV-screen coordinates.
- The original [1997 Japanese §2.1](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ssddv25/segahtml/hard/vdp2/hon/p02_10_j.htm), [manual correction history](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ssddv25/segahtml/hard/vdp2/history.htm) and applicable STN corrections govern discrepancies with older material.

Document the distinction between image/coefficient coordinates, output-dot coordinates and acquisition timing. Establish any changed acquisition cadence from affirmative specification evidence; where physical phases are unspecified, retain an explicit deterministic convention. Spatial resolution alone does not prove a physical fetch or retention phase.

AI implementation agents may correct an AI-authored technical assumption using exact primary references and rationale, updating this Issue accordingly without human confirmation. Preserve the required hardware behavior and meaningful independent validation.

## Context and reproduction

Inspected local and upstream `main` both identify `dacd8b18e2009fb25ed4bcd6fc719d9f796f16f6`. No open Issues were returned. The supplied main build remains in progress; no success or failure is inferred.

Relevant implementation:

- `src/vdp2/rotation.rs:200`: horizontal coefficient addressing.
- `src/vdp2/rotation.rs:264`: matrix coordinate calculation.
- `src/vdp2/rotation.rs:363`: shared rotation sampling and parameter selection.
- `src/vdp2/fetch.rs:365`: scheduled rotation acquisition.
- `src/timing.rs:199`: output-dot deadlines.
- `src/vdp2/rotation_fetch_tests.rs:288`: existing high-resolution test.

Reproduce with static, distinct neighboring source pixels, identity parameters, no mosaic/window/color effects and valid rotation-bank assignments. Compare 320→640 and 352→704 mode pairs. Check the complete source span, including the right edge, rather than only a few repeated colors.

Scope is high-resolution rotation-background sampling and its acquisition/composition integration. Half-line interlace, general coefficient-table bus scheduling, unrelated video effects and other chips remain separate work.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Write a primary-derived contract covering output-to-rotation coordinate mapping, coefficient progression, parameter-window coordinates and acquisition conventions. Reconcile applicable corrections; distinguish documented behavior from inferred or unspecified timing.
- [ ] Add independent static pixel/address vectors that fail against the inherited unscaled-X behavior. At identity, verify paired output pixels and the complete 320/352-source-dot span in 640/704 output modes. Expected values must come from authored source patterns and specification equations, without production address helpers or captured emulator goldens.
- [ ] Correct both RBG0 parameter selections, RBG0 tile/bitmap paths and RBG1’s fixed-bank tile path. Cover legal high-resolution color formats, character/name boundaries, signed or fractional horizontal increments and a nonzero horizontal coefficient increment with independently expected indices/results.
- [ ] Verify windows and parameter switching at an odd output-dot boundary so an incorrect global X scaling cannot pass. Preserve normal-background and VDP1 composition coordinates, palette interpretation, priorities and existing format restrictions.
- [ ] Preserve retained scheduled operands and missing-fetch behavior. Test controlled memory changes around acquisition boundaries, advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000, passive debugger inspection, new fields and reset cancellation against the documented phase convention. Do not repair scheduled misses through live snapshot reads.
- [ ] Add or extend original MIT-licensed SH-2 fixtures that configure the documented clock/display modes and construct their own images, names, palettes, matrices and coefficients through guest instructions/MMIO. Native Machine tests must check full diagnostic image regions and guest-computed records for 640/704 output, RBG0 and RBG1, changed source/parameter operands, omitted-enable controls and repeated cold boots.
- [ ] Execute identical fixture bytes in production browser Wasm under `/saturn-rust/`, checking dimensions, independent expected pixels, guest records and actual Canvas output. Register reproducible source/media checks in the existing workflow. Host code must not supply guest results or rendered pixels.
- [ ] Preserve existing tests and demonstrations, including normal-resolution rotation acquisition, one-shot reloads, sprite rotation, video-write ordering, Star Collector, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab. Any incorrect historical expectation must receive a primary-backed replacement retaining its original regression purpose; do not delete coverage to obtain green tests.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native and wasm32 Clippy with warnings denied, registered fixture/media reproduction checks, `sh scripts/build-web.sh` and the complete extended `npm run test:browser`, with no required skips.
- [ ] Update `docs/vdp2-rotation-fetch.md`, architecture/conformance entries and a validation record with exact primary references, executed results, remaining conventions and an actual inherited-behavior negative control. Keep this explicitly partial under #17.

## Optional validation

None required. Existing lawful compatibility evidence may be reported separately; commercial-game compatibility remains unverified without actual testing.

## Required post-merge verification

None.

All unmet #17 CPU/peripheral, multiprocessor/bus/reset/timing, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and integrated-validation requirements remain mandatory. This increment does not establish hardware completion. Do not reopen historical trackers or require personal firmware, commercial media, physical hardware, human approval, live Pages inspection or administrative-closure investigation.
